observations.statement: PS-123 requires inline visualizer v2 to use a sandboxed iframe or equivalent isolation boundary, starts with an empty library allowlist, subjects named candidate libraries to approval evidence, denies remote and parent-access vectors, uses the CV-300 isolated webview adapter for Rust + Slint, validates four bridge-message properties before host execution, and defers Tone.js and Wavesurfer.

PS-123 acceptance requires evidence for each allowed library, native/iframe bridge policy parity, and denial of parent DOM/localStorage and unvetted network/CDN/import access; its validation surfaces include plan-index validation and sandbox/library-denial fixtures.
PS-123 declares dependencies on ACD-427 and CV-300 and unblocks F3-404 and ATS-015.

PS-124 requires destination enablement plus live-send authority, confines provider secrets to OS credential references or equivalent custody, redacts a broad set of sensitive notification content, and prevents external dismissal from resolving PM blockers or canonical conditions.
PS-124 acceptance limits receipts and UI surfaces to secret references or masked values and preserves canonical blocker state; it also states that preview does not imply live-send authority.
PS-124 depends on CV-298, unblocks SP-222, F3-405, RAP-039, and ATS-016, and names a notification secret-custody/live-send fixture.

PS-125 limits Auto Apply trust to a configured upstream source/channel, delegates credential and sign-in authority to the underlying provider/account/Multi-Account owner, and requires permission/authority plus diagnostic redaction for probes, quota checks, costed fallback, and generated-adapter activation.

PS-125 acceptance rejects untrusted forks, arbitrary URLs, and arbitrary scripts, makes default refresh metadata/catalog-only without quota spend, delegates credential custody, and requires explicit authority with redacted evidence for live probes or quota-spending checks.

PS-125 declares no dependencies or unblocked PlanUnits; its preserved tokens name a configured vava-nessa/free-coding-models source/channel, while its negative constraints reject arbitrary upstream execution and raw-secret exposure.

PS-126 fails containerized-host security closed, separates discovery/configuration/GUI/profile selection from execution approval, requires enumerated trust, permission, policy, FileSafe, target-approval, redaction, and receipt gates before high-risk effects, and represents policy blocks as blocked rather than failed.

PS-126 acceptance binds every high-risk approval to target, profile/capability, runtime family, permission snapshot, trust policy, and expected receipts; blocked outcomes preserve diagnostic/action fields, and raw secrets are excluded from all named surfaces.

PS-126 depends on CV-303, CV-304, F2-194, and RM-048, unblocks CRAU-091, EP-109, T-166, ATS-019, and RAP-042, and forbids generic approval or hidden defaults from enabling privileged or remote effects.

PS-127 requires model-independent runtime enforcement through an AutonomyCeilingReceipt after provider/tool parsing and before execution, with the runtime rather than model/tool payload deciding whether mutation proceeds.

PS-127 acceptance blocks a malicious or buggy requires_approval=false tool call in Plan/Read-only mode, requires pre-run terminal approval to display command, cwd, mutation class, and effective mode ceiling, and classifies the PlanUnit as GUI-related.

The AutonomyCeilingReceipt contract enumerates receipt, correlation, mode, source, mutation, decision, reason, permission-snapshot, timestamp, and enforcement-point fields; stores events as autonomy.ceiling_checked with a redb projection by attempt_id; and orders parse, schema validation, autonomy, permission/FileSafe, and dispatch.
PS-127 depends on PDS-003 and PNC-001; its listed validation surfaces are two plan/ledger validators followed by repetitions of two acceptance statements.

candidate_findings.title: Equivalent visualizer isolation is not testably defined
candidate_findings.statement: PS-123 permits an equivalent isolation boundary but does not state the minimum isolation capabilities, forbidden iframe flags, or equivalence oracle that a non-iframe implementation must satisfy.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can select materially different isolation mechanisms while each claims equivalence, weakening the sandbox-escape boundary and making acceptance nondeterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Bridge nonce and invalid-message lifecycle are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: PS-123 names origin_nonce, artifact identity, method schema, and permission state validation but does not define nonce issuance, binding, lifetime, replay rejection, message direction, or the required failure response before host execution.
candidate_findings.impact: A bridge can validate field presence yet remain vulnerable to replay, confused-deputy routing, or inconsistent fail-open/fail-closed behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Library owner approval lacks an authority contract
candidate_findings.statement: PS-123 requires owner approval and approval evidence without identifying the approving authority, approval record shape, scope, expiry, revocation, or reapproval trigger after an upgrade or removal decision.
candidate_findings.impact: Library admission and continued use can vary by implementation, and stale approvals may survive security or version changes.

candidate_findings.title: Notification live-send authority has no state or lease semantics
candidate_findings.statement: PS-124 requires destination enablement and explicit live-send authority but does not define the authority state, grantor, destination/account binding, scope, lifetime, revocation, or transition from preview/test to live delivery.
candidate_findings.impact: A preview, test send, reconnect, or destination change can be interpreted inconsistently and may enable unintended external disclosure.

candidate_findings.title: Equivalent secret custody is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: PS-124 allows OS credential references or equivalent secret custody but gives no normative properties or acceptance test for the equivalent mechanism.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can label weaker storage as equivalent, undermining the otherwise strict secret-reference and masking requirements.

candidate_findings.title: Free Models trusted-source verification is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: PS-125 relies on a configured trusted upstream source/channel and rejects untrusted forks, but does not define the authoritative source identity, channel pin, authenticity proof, redirect/fork handling, or update and rollback rules in normative behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Auto Apply trust decisions can diverge or accept a substituted source despite satisfying the prose-level configured-source check.

candidate_findings.title: Free Models permission authority is not operationally defined
candidate_findings.statement: PS-125 says probes, quota-spending checks, costed fallback, and generated-adapter activation require the relevant permission/authority state, without naming that state, its owner, grant scope, expiry, revocation, or denial result.
candidate_findings.impact: Quota spend and adapter activation can be authorized differently across implementations, including through an overly broad or stale grant.

candidate_findings.title: Costed fallback and adapter activation lack acceptance coverage
candidate_findings.statement: PS-125 makes costed fallback and generated-adapter activation authority-gated, but its acceptance criteria and named fixtures cover source trust, credential custody, refresh, probes, and quota checks without an oracle for either costed fallback or adapter activation.
candidate_findings.impact: Two consequential side-effect paths can ship without evidence that their authority and redaction obligations are enforced.

candidate_findings.title: Container host gate composition and precedence are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: PS-126 lists trust, permission snapshot, approval scope, network, secret, destructive-command, FileSafe, target approval, redaction, and receipt prerequisites but does not define their types, evaluators, precedence, missing-value behavior, conflict resolution, or deterministic decision output.
candidate_findings.impact: Different executors can produce different allow/block decisions for the same host action and policy snapshot despite the fail-closed statement.

candidate_findings.title: Target-bound approvals lack freshness and replay rules
candidate_findings.statement: PS-126 binds high-risk approvals to target and permission/trust context but does not define approval lifetime, single-use versus reusable scope, invalidation on target/profile/policy/snapshot change, duplicate dispatch handling, or concurrent-use behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: A stale or replayed approval can authorize a changed target or repeated destructive action, and retries can create duplicate external effects.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked host outcomes lack transition semantics
candidate_findings.statement: PS-126 specifies blocked_reason_code, blocked scope, policy source, required action, allowed_action_ids, and evidence references but does not define which action transitions the operation, whether reevaluation is automatic, or how cancellation and retry preserve or replace the blocked record.
candidate_findings.impact: Consumers cannot implement a consistent blocked-to-ready, blocked-to-cancelled, or retry lifecycle, and receipts may lose causal continuity.

candidate_findings.title: Privileged DinD default is only implied by a future fixture
candidate_findings.statement: PS-126 names a future privileged DinD default-disabled fixture, while the accepted behavior and acceptance criteria do not explicitly state the default-disabled state or its enablement authority.
candidate_findings.impact: The fixture name and implementation can disagree, leaving a high-risk default dependent on builder interpretation.

candidate_findings.title: Autonomy ceiling decision policy is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: PS-127 defines requested_mode, effective_mode, mutation_class, ceiling_source_ref, and allow/block/require_approval decisions but does not define the mode hierarchy, mutation classes, authoritative ceiling-source resolution, or the mapping that produces a decision.
candidate_findings.impact: The runtime is declared authoritative but lacks a deterministic policy contract, so adapters or executors can disagree on whether a mutation is below, at, or above the ceiling.

candidate_findings.title: Require-approval continuation and recheck behavior are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The receipt decision includes require_approval and the order places the autonomy check before permission/FileSafe and dispatch, but the window does not define whether dispatch pauses, which approval satisfies it, whether a new receipt is emitted, or which state must be revalidated after approval.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation may dispatch on stale mode or permission state, skip a second ceiling check, or produce evidence that cannot prove the final authorization path.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt correlation and projection cardinality are ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: AutonomyCeilingReceipt makes tool_call_ref and provider_message_ref optional while storage projects autonomy.ceiling_checked by attempt_id, without defining one-versus-many projection semantics, overwrite rules, uniqueness, idempotency, or ordering for multiple tool calls in one attempt.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrent or retried calls can collide in the projection or become impossible to correlate to the exact decision that gated dispatch.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime autonomy enforcement lacks an executable acceptance oracle
candidate_findings.statement: PS-127's validation list contains plan-index and ledger validators plus repeated prose acceptance statements, but names no runtime fixture or schema/event/projection check for AutonomyCeilingReceipt creation, ordering, persistence, or malicious-payload blocking.
candidate_findings.impact: The PlanUnit can pass its listed validators without executable evidence that the runtime enforcement point or receipt contract exists.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: PS-123 explicitly defaults the library allowlist to empty, denies named remote/import/parent-access paths, and defers Tone.js and Wavesurfer rather than implicitly approving them.
PS-123 explicitly requires exact library provenance/security/performance/fallback/upgrade evidence and native bridge parity with iframe/postMessage restrictions.

PS-124 explicitly constrains secret custody and masking across receipts and UI, broadly enumerates prohibited disclosure content, and prevents external notification dismissal from changing canonical blocker truth.
PS-125 explicitly rejects untrusted forks, arbitrary URLs, and arbitrary scripts, delegates provider credential custody, and makes default refresh metadata/catalog-only without quota spend.
PS-126 explicitly fails closed and states that discovery, configuration, GUI availability, or profile selection is not execution approval.
PS-126 explicitly binds high-risk approval to target and permission/trust context, preserves structured blocked fields, and prohibits raw secrets from every named host surface.

PS-127 explicitly places model-independent enforcement after parsing and before execution, assigns the mutation decision to runtime, and tests the specific requires_approval=false Plan/Read-only bypass case at the acceptance level.
The window explicitly enumerates AutonomyCeilingReceipt fields, its event payload and redb projection location, and the enforcement order through dispatch.

unknowns.statement: The behavioral contracts of ACD-427, CV-300, CV-298, CV-303, CV-304, F2-194, RM-048, PDS-003, PNC-001, and the named unblocked consumers are unknown within the allowed window.
The identities and authority chains for visualizer library owners and notification live-send grantors are not stated in the window.
The exact configured Free Models source/channel value and the mechanism that proves an upstream is trusted are not established by normative behavior in the window.
The schemas, sources of authority, defaults, and versioning rules for the container host trust and policy objects are not stated in the window.
The allowed requested/effective mode values, mutation-class taxonomy, and ceiling_source_ref resolution semantics are not stated in the window.
The omission semantics for optional receipt fields and the cardinality of the attempt_id redb projection are not stated in the window.
Accessibility behavior for the pre-run terminal approval display is not specified in the window, although PS-127 is GUI-related and requires four visible values.

General cancellation, retry, idempotency, and concurrency semantics are not stated for the visualizer bridge, notification delivery, Free Models live operations, container host actions, or autonomy-ceiling events.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote:
Inline visualizer v2 runs in a sandboxed iframe or equivalent isolation boundary with default library allowlist
  empty. Candidate libraries such as Chart.js, D3, Vega-Lite, ECharts, Plotly, and vis-network require exact
  package/version, bundled asset, SHA-256/SRI, license, security, performance, capability, fallback, upgrade/removal,
  and owner approval before use. Remote CDN loading, cdnjs/jsdelivr/unpkg, dynamic imports, unvetted network access,
  undeclared runtime script injection, `allow-same-origin`, parent document scraping, and raw parent localStorage are
  denied. Rust + Slint builds use the PM-owned isolated webview adapter from CV-300, with postMessage-equivalent
  bridge messages validated for origin_nonce, visualizer_artifact_id, method schema, and permission state before host
  execution. Tone.js and Wavesurfer remain deferred until separately approved.

- Default visualizer library allowlist is empty.
  - Every allowed library has exact version, bundled asset, hash/SRI, license, security, performance, capability, fallback, upgrade/removal, and owner approval evidence.
  - Native webview adapter bridge calls enforce the same sandbox, origin/nonce, method-schema, and no-parent-access policy as iframe/postMessage calls.
  - Sandboxed visualizers cannot reach parent DOM/localStorage or unvetted network/CDN/import paths.

Notification destinations that send to Slack, Discord, generic webhook, ntfy, Pushover, Telegram, or other remote

  private paths, full prompts, full logs, screenshots, raw diff bodies, or unredacted identities. External notification
  dismissal never resolves PM blocked episodes or canonical conditions.

- Live test-send and remote delivery require an enabled destination plus explicit authority.

  - External provider dismissal cannot resolve canonical PM blocker state.

Live probes, quota-spending checks, costed fallback, and generated-adapter activation require the relevant permission/authority state and must be redacted in diagnostics.

  - Free Models setup delegates credential custody to the underlying provider/account flow.
  - Default refresh is metadata/catalog-only and does not spend quota by default.

Containerized-host security fails closed. Discovery, configuration, GUI availability, or a selected host profile is
  not execution approval. Host operations require scoped trust state, permission_snapshot_id, approval_scope_key,
  network_access_policy, secret_access_policy, destructive_command_policy, FileSafe scope, target-bound approvals,
  redaction, and receipt logging before mutation, attach, port exposure, image push, remote SSH, Kubernetes, Unraid,
  registry write, Docker socket, privileged DinD, secret injection, or external side effect. Blocked permission,
  FileSafe, trust, policy, network, and test-gap outcomes remain `blocked != failed` and expose allowed_action_ids plus
  blocked_reason_code rather than silent failure.

- Discovery/configuration cannot grant execution, attach, expose-port, push, remote, Kubernetes, Unraid, registry, Docker socket, privileged DinD, or secret-injection authority.
  - Every high-risk host action binds approval to target, host profile/capability, runtime family, permission snapshot, trust policy, and expected receipts.
  - Blocked outcomes preserve blocked_reason_code, blocked scope, policy source, required action, allowed_action_ids, and evidence refs.
  - Raw secrets never appear in host profiles, prompts, GUI, logs, receipts, exports, diagnostics, or evidence.

gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: User-visible GUI, built-in terminal, accessibility, visual, multimodal, or desktop surface is directly implicated.

`AutonomyCeilingReceipt` fields: `receipt_id`, `schema_version`, `attempt_id`, `run_id?`, `requested_mode`, `effective_mode`, `ceiling_source_ref`, `tool_call_ref?`, `provider_message_ref?`, `mutation_class`, `decision` (`allow`, `block`, `require_approval`), `blocked_reason_code?`, `permission_snapshot_id`, `created_at_utc`, and `enforcement_point` (`post_parse_pre_execution`). Storage location is the canonical event stream as an `autonomy.ceiling_checked` payload with redb projection by `attempt_id`. Enforcement order is provider/tool parse, schema validation, autonomy ceiling check, permission/FileSafe check, then dispatch.
